items.followUp: Define ionization energy and electron affinity.

rubric.why: Electron affinity concerns the energy change when an isolated gaseous atom accepts an electron.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity in terms of a gaseous atom accepting an electron and the associated energy change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the gaseous atom accepting an electron and the associated energy change.

rubric.why: Electronegativity describes the attraction exerted by an atom on shared electrons in a molecule.
rubric.description: Defines electronegativity as the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract shared electrons towards itself.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the attraction of shared electrons.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy change when an isolated gaseous atom accepts an electron to form a negative ion.
Electronegativity is the ability of an atom in a molecule to attract the shared pair of electrons towards itself.

rubric.why: A duplet is a stable arrangement with two electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: Defines the duplet rule as stability with two electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom is stable with two outer-shell electrons.

rubric.why: An octet is a stable arrangement with eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.description: Defines the octet rule as stability with eight electrons in the outermost shell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an atom is stable with eight outer-shell electrons.

modelAnswer: The duplet rule states that an atom is stable when its outermost shell contains two electrons.
The octet rule states that an atom is stable when its outermost shell contains eight electrons.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example of diffusion in a liquid.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the spreading of gas particles from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.description: Defines gas diffusion as the spreading of gas particles from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the definition, including the direction of movement from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: The smell of perfume spreading through a room is a valid example of gas diffusion.
rubric.description: Gives a correct example of gas diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as the smell of perfume spreading through a room.

modelAnswer: Diffusion of a gas is the spreading of its particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
For example, the smell of perfume spreads through a room by diffusion.
